items_missed: No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' — the call went straight from 'How can I help you?' into date and address collection with no roadmap, no 10–15 minute timeframe, and no confirmation ask.

Never asked 'how are you today?' — and this was the one call where it was free. Sophia opened with 'Apologies for my voice in advance. I'm a little sick right now' and got 'No worries.' No acknowledgment, no empathy, no 'sorry you're under the weather.'

Availability was never checked proactively — Sophia had to ask 'do you all have availability on Wednesday?' nine minutes in. Chris had the date from the second minute and never volunteered the answer.

Save Your Ass speech never delivered — a total miss on 10 points, and Sophia teed it up herself: 'everything's kind of laying on the ground there's nothing stacked high... we did not do a good job using the space wisely.' She was describing a unit that could consolidate to roughly half its footprint. Chris's answer was 'Oh, you're good.'

No Worries Damage Coverage never explained. 'Insurance' was named once as a line item bundled into the hourly rate — the customer has no idea she has $2,000 of repair/replace/reimburse coverage on a king mattress, a sectional, and 30 boxes.
On-Time Guarantee never mentioned — and he was actively selling urgency ('the sooner you let us know the better'), which is exactly where the guarantee belongs.

No sense-check anywhere in the call. No 'does that make sense?' after the pricing block, after the clock explanation, or after the estimate — three separate places where the rubric asks for one and the customer got a monologue instead.

Walk distance never probed on a storage-facility move. 'Depending on the access between the units' was the closest he came — he never asked how far the 10x30 is from truck parking, whether the unit is interior or drive-up, or how far the 10x5 is from the 10x30. On a storage job that is the single biggest time variable and it went unmeasured.

Specialty/heavy items never asked about. The washer and dryer came up from the customer's side only, and he never flagged them as a time factor even though moving them to the second unit is part of the scope.
No trip fee discussion at all — see the live-risk note in the coaching field; origin 78717 is the Round Rock corridor.
Packing services never offered or priced. He asserted it rather than asking: 'we're moved for a storage. We're not packing up anything in the boxes.'
No equivalents or volume reference (school bus, truckloads) used to help her sanity-check a 90%-full 10x30 against a 5–7 hour estimate.
Ecobox / Sparefoot referral missed despite being unusually relevant — she is downsizing to a 10x5 at the same facility and using roughly 30 boxes.

Booking never actually attempted. He described how booking works ('if you want to book, we just book it and send you a confirmation email') but never asked for it. No 'we have Wednesday the 30th open — want me to lock that in for you right now?'
No BOLDED-details framing for the confirmation email and no 'reply with any corrections' — the email was positioned as a quote to respond to if she wants to book, not as a record for her to verify.
Business hours never given, only the channels (call, text, email).
Customer's name used essentially once, and only while spelling her email address back — short of the 3+ standard on a 9.6-minute call.
top_strength: The pricing-and-clock block is the best thing on this call and it was fast — Chris delivered the whole structure in about sixty seconds without losing the customer. He opened correctly with 'Our pricing super simple,' gave the rate cleanly against the specific date ('$104 an hour for mover, we send a two man team, so it's $208 per hour'), then ran the full inclusions list (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, pads, moving blankets, shrink wrap, tools for reassembly) and closed it with a genuinely strong no-hidden-fees pitch: 'no elevator stair step fee, no heavy item fee, no special item fee. Literally no other fees.' The clock followed immediately and correctly stated — on-site start, two-and-a-half hour minimum, fifteen-minute prorated increments, 'you're charged just for time used.' His mid-call recap was also a real strength: 'so we've been transferring stuff from the 10x30 to the 10x5 on site and then taking the rest of it to the apartment at Harmon, on the first floor' — he caught and confirmed a two-part scope that is easy to lose, and she confirmed it back.
coaching_note: Highest-leverage fix: Sophia handed you the Save Your Ass speech on a plate and you passed on it. When she said 'we did not do a good job using the space wisely' and described everything lying loose on the floor, the answer was: 'That actually matters for your bill — prep before move day means a shorter move and a lower total. If you can get the loose stuff into boxes, consolidate the small items, and take a carload of anything that fits in your car, you'll knock real time off the clock. Does that make sense?' On a job billed at $208 an hour, that one speech was worth more to her than anything else you said, and it protects your estimate at the same time. Second priority: you told her 'insurance' was included and moved on — say the actual differentiator out loud ('$2,000 No Worries Damage Coverage, and we repair, replace, or reimburse accidental damage in-house'), then add the On-Time Guarantee, because you were already selling urgency and that is where it lands. Third, you never asked for the booking — she said 'this is really good to know, thank you so much' and you replied by confirming her email address; 'We have plenty of openings on the 30th, there's no deposit and no cancellation fee — want me to just lock it in for you now?' books that call. LIVE BUSINESS RISK: the origin is 13126 Ranch Road 620 N, Austin 78717, which is the Round Rock / Avery Ranch corridor — another quote graded from the same day carries a $75 trip fee to Round Rock, and you quoted this job with no trip fee mentioned at all. Verify the service zone and correct the emailed quote before she books, or that is either a margin hit or a move-day surprise on a customer who was told 'literally no other fees.' SECOND RISK — estimate accuracy: 5–7 hours for a 90%-full, badly-stacked 10x30 plus an on-site transfer of the washer and dryer to a second unit looks light, and you leaned it lighter still with 'it's gonna be close to that if not less.' You also anchored the range to 'a typical two bedroom apartment,' which is not what this is. If that job runs eight-plus hours it is a textbook underquote on the exact metric we are trying to move.
phone_presence_notes: Efficient and easy to buy from — the customer ended genuinely pleased ('this is super helpful... I appreciate your time') and he did affirm her well in spots ('that's super helpful,' 'Oh, you're good') — but the language was transactional, her name was barely used, there was no humor or rapport moment, and he stepped straight past her opening 'I'm a little sick right now' with a flat 'No worries.'
